tex_content.html:
Theorem
[Cartan's Fixed-Point Theorem] ↗ lem:unique-minimal-enclosing-ball 1. ch12:12.17

Let $(M,g)$ be a Cartan--Hadamard manifold and let a compact Lie group $G$ act smoothly and isometrically on $M$. Then some $p_0\in M$ is fixed by every element of $G$.
Proof

\sketch For $q_0\in M$, the orbit $S=G\cdot q_0$ is compact. If it is a singleton, its point is fixed. Otherwise, let $p_0$ be its unique 1-center. Every $\varphi \in G$ preserves $S$ and sends its minimum enclosing ball to a ball of the same radius centered at $\varphi \cdot p_0$. Uniqueness of the 1-center implies $\varphi \cdot p_0=p_0$.

□

An element $\varphi $ of a group is a torsion element if $\varphi ^k=1$ for some integer $k>1$. A group is torsion-free if its only torsion element is the identity.
